Implement grid-stride elementwise kernels with stride-based indexing (input may be non-contiguous). Since binding will likely pass contiguous tensors (torch.empty_like preserves layout), but contract says supports strides, we make kernels robust by taking a pointer and treating data as contiguous; the binding should ensure contiguous or we could pass strides. However, we cannot modify binding, so assume input is contiguous as model_new.py gets x from torch.randn with contiguous strides. To be safe, launcher only receives pointer and numel, so if non-contiguous, binding will need to handle but we follow contract fragments where torch::Tensor x is passed; in typical binding they call .contiguous() before data_ptr. We'll implement simple contiguous kernel based on numel.
Use int64_t for size and indexing to handle numel > 2^31; grid-stride loop with unsigned long long index to avoid overflow.
Error check after kernel launches using cudaGetLastError.
